verses.1:1: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
verses.1:2: Grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: We ought to give thanks to God always concerning you, brothers, just as it is fitting, because your faith grows exceedingly and the love of each and every one of you toward one another abounds,
verses.1:4: so that we ourselves boast in you among the churches of God regarding your steadfastness and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions that you are enduring,
verses.1:5: which is evidence of the righteous judgment of God, so that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer,
verses.1:6: since indeed it is righteous with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you,
verses.1:7: and to you who are afflicted, relief together with us at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of His power
verses.1:8: in flaming fire, inflicting vengeance on those who do not know God and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus.
verses.1:9: Such ones will pay the penalty, eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His might,
verses.1:10: when He comes to be glorified in His saints and to be marveled at among all who have believed—because our testimony to you was believed—on that day.
verses.1:11: To this end we also pray always for you, that our God may count you worthy of the calling, and fulfill every desire for goodness and work of faith in power,
verses.1:12: so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2:1: Now we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to Him,
verses.2:2: not to be quickly shaken from your reason nor to be alarmed, whether by a spirit, or by a word, or by a letter as if through us, to the effect that the day of the Lord is already present.
verses.2:3: Let no one deceive you in any way; for it will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,
verses.2:4: who opposes and exalts himself over every so-called god or object of worship, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself to be God.
verses.2:5: Do you not remember that while I was still with you, I used to tell you these things?
verses.2:6: And now you know what restrains him, so that he will be revealed in his own time.
verses.2:7: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who restrains at present does so until he is out of the way.
verses.2:8: And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of His mouth and bring to nothing by the appearance of His coming.
verses.2:9: That one's coming is according to the working of Satan, with all power and signs and wonders of falsehood,
verses.2:10: and with all deception of unrighteousness for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved.
verses.2:11: And because of this, God sends them a working of delusion, so that they will believe the lie,
verses.2:12: in order that all may be judged who did not believe the truth, but took pleasure in unrighteousness.
verses.2:13: But we ought to give thanks to God always concerning you, brothers loved by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning for salvation through sanctification by the Spirit and faith in the truth,
verses.2:14: to which He called you through our gospel, for the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2:15: So then, brothers, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions that you were taught, whether by word or by our letter.
verses.2:16: Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself and God our Father, who loved us and gave eternal encouragement and good hope in grace,
verses.2:17: encourage your hearts and establish them in every good work and word.
verses.3:1: Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, just as it also is with you,
verses.3:2: and that we may be rescued from perverse and evil men; for faith does not belong to all.
verses.3:3: But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
verses.3:4: And we have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that what we command, you both do and will do.
verses.3:5: Now may the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the steadfastness of Christ.
verses.3:6: Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you keep away from every brother who walks in a disorderly way and not according to the tradition that they received from us.
verses.3:7: For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we did not act in a disorderly way among you,
verses.3:8: nor did we eat bread free of charge from anyone, but with toil and hardship, working night and day so as not to be a burden to any of you;
verses.3:9: not because we do not have the right, but in order to give ourselves as a pattern to you, so that you might imitate us.
verses.3:10: For even when we were with you, we used to command you this: "If anyone is not willing to work, neither let him eat."
verses.3:11: For we hear that some among you are walking in a disorderly way, working at nothing, but acting as busybodies.
verses.3:12: Now such people we command and urge in the Lord Jesus Christ that, working with quietness, they eat their own bread.
verses.3:13: But as for you, brothers, do not lose heart in doing good.
verses.3:14: And if anyone does not obey our word through this letter, take note of that person and do not associate with him, so that he may feel ashamed.
verses.3:15: Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
verses.3:16: Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace continually in every way. The Lord be with you all.
verses.3:17: The greeting is by my own hand, Paul's, which is a sign in every letter; this is how I write.
verses.3:18: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.

notes.1:8: The phrase "in flaming fire" (literally "in a fire of flame") can be connected either with the revelation of the Lord Jesus in 1:7 or with the inflicting of vengeance in 1:8.
notes.1:9: The preposition "away from" (Greek apo) may express either eternal separation from the Lord's presence or the source from which the destruction comes.
notes.1:12: The Greek phrase "of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ" shares a single definite article, allowing it to be read either of two persons or of one ("our God and Lord, Jesus Christ").
notes.2:3: The Greek clause is elliptical, omitting the main verb ("it will not come") before the condition; "rebellion" translates apostasia (also rendered "apostasy").
notes.2:6: Paul refers to the unnamed restrainer with a neuter participle here ("what restrains") and a masculine participle in 2:7 ("the one who restrains"), where the verb in the main clause is also elliptical.
notes.2:13: The critical text reads ap' arches ("from the beginning"); a well-attested manuscript variant reads aparchen ("as firstfruits").
notes.2:17: The optative verbs "encourage" and "establish" are grammatically singular in Greek despite the compound subject of Christ and God the Father in 2:16, highlighting their unified action.
notes.3:3: The Greek phrase tou ponerou can be taken as masculine ("the evil one") or neuter ("evil").
notes.3:5: Both "the love of God" and "the steadfastness of Christ" are ambiguous genitives that may refer to God's own love and Christ's endurance or to the believers' love for God and Christ-like endurance.
notes.3:6: Greek ataktos ("in a disorderly way") denotes acting out of order or shirking duty, here tied to idleness; the critical text reads the third-person plural "they received" rather than the variant "you received."
notes.3:11: The Greek employs a pun contrasting ergazomenous ("working") with periergazomenous ("acting as busybodies" or "meddling").
